title: Positive eigenvalues of the relative SU(2) BFSS Hamiltonian

issues.location: Introduction, definition of H (closure of q on gauge-invariant C_c^infty)
issues.description: The theorem concerns the self-adjoint operator obtained by closing the supercharge form on gauge-invariant C_c^infty, which is a Friedrichs-type realization. The refutation of the BFSS statement therefore applies to this realization specifically. The paper states this choice openly; it is not an error.
issues.evidence: 'Let H be the nonnegative self-adjoint operator associated with its closure ... This is the relative SU(2) BFSS Hamiltonian considered here.'

coverage: Read the whole paper (all 4 sections, 888 lines of LaTeX) and checked each step by hand. Lemma 2.1: (1/16)ΣA² = -Δ/2 and (1/16)ΣW² = V under the normalization {θ,θ}=δ; B is Hermitian and linear in x. Lemma 2.2: the Spin(9) and gauge actions commute, P_λ preserves the core, and the subspace H_λ reduces H. Lemma 3.1: the B4→D4 branching proof by character determinant, including the half-integral case and t_4 ≤ 0; this gives ν_1 ≥ λ_2. Lemma 3.2: restricting the finite-dimensional G-span of Ψ to a slice intertwines K_u. Lemma 3.3: the oscillator levels are r(n+8) after the substitution ξ = √(2r)z; for degree ≤ n, weights have ν_1 ≤ n+M, which excludes levels n ≤ m. Proposition 3.4: the slice/Fubini bound, averaging over colours with Σ|x^a| ≥ |x|, closure to the full form domain, and Rellich compactness plus a tail estimate. Section 4: the Fock vacuum line is gauge invariant; P is gauge invariant, nonzero, and a highest vector of weight 2(ε1+ε2); P^k v is highest of weight λ, so H_λ is infinite-dimensional. Constants are robust because m is free. No sympy run was needed, since every computation was short enough to check by hand.
main_claim: For the relative SU(2) BFSS Hamiltonian, defined as the closure of the gauge-invariant supercharge form, there are infinitely many positive eigenvalues E_j → ∞ with L² eigenvectors. Spin(9) sectors with large λ_2 exclude the low transverse oscillator levels, which confines those sectors (compact resolvent, trivial kernel), and infinitely many of these sectors are infinite-dimensional.
sibling_notes: Same family as 'The unique threshold bound state of the SU(N) BFSS model' (rank 105, no_gap_found). This paper does not depend on that companion; it is self-contained. The mechanism is consistent with the valley picture: in the valley, only K_u types with bounded ν_1 are available at low energy, and interlacing then forbids large λ_2.
